 During a candid new sit-down with Ice Cube and Mike Epps, Katt Williams revealed the story behind how he and Kevin Hart finally called a truce, along with a fresh round of unfiltered takes that only he could deliver. From talking about his past 14 gun charges and rumors of him fighting after shows to his thoughts about Steve Harvey and Cedric the Entertainer, Williams held nothing back in yet another viral interview.
 The Ohio native appeared on episode two of Ice Cube and Mike Epps’ podcast “Listen & Laugh” on Saturday, where he spoke about a variety of topics, including his long-standing beef with fellow comedian Kevin Hart and how he and Hart are now actually…friends!
 During the interview (which has over three million views in two days), Epps referenced Williams’s surprise appearance as a guest roaster on Netflix’s “The Roast of Kevin Hart” in May, where he said Williams “told the truth” about Hart, who appeared unfazed by it all. 
 “Hey, this is my friend you’re talking about,” Williams interjected. “Sorry, Kev.” After a brief laugh, Epps noted that despite their rocky history, he was grateful Hart called him to be in a movie together after years of rumored beef. The conversation led to Williams explaining how he and Hart made amends.
 “I didn’t like the guy,” Williams answered when asked how he felt when Hart called him to appear in a film together. “And I had reasons that I felt that way. […] I had reasons I didn’t like him, but when he contacted me, there was probably a list in my head of 15 things a motherf***er would have to say to get me to be off from on-sight, to we could be good. To his credit—or the credit of him and Netflix or whatever it was—he said everything I needed to hear him say. So he gave an apology that was worthy of being forgiven. There was no working involved in the conversation that we were having, but then, once that was behind us, now we can do whatever the work is that’s necessary.” 
 Katt Williams had to remind Mike Epps that he’s FRIENDS with Kevin Hart now after Mike started throwing RANDOM SHOTS at him and saying he DOESN’T LIKE HIM 😭💀
“This is my friend you talking about, easy… Sorry Kev” pic.twitter.com/3YgiKNa5bc 
— Killa 🌺 (@KillaKreww) November 14, 2026 
 But that’s not all. Williams also dropped more bombshells in his interview, including his other comedy beefs.
 He’s Going Straight for Steve Harvey’s Knees
 In his viral interview with Shannon Sharpe in January 2024, Williams made it clear he is not a fan of Steve Harvey, claiming he plagiarized Mark Curry’s role as Mark Cooper in “Hangin’ with Mr. Cooper” on his series, “The Steve Harvey Show.”
 RELATED: A Year Later, Was Katt Williams Right? Here Are All the Celebs He Dragged 
 When Epps asked whether Williams would be nice to Harvey if they ran into each other, Williams didn’t mince words. “Steve recently did an interview where he said he’s with the smoke. So, if I see Steve Harvey, I’m going straight for his knees.”
 Did He Chase Tyler Perry With a Broomstick?
 Mike Epps recalls a story Eddie Murphy told him about Katt Williams and Suge Knight showing up unannounced at his house early one morning, and Katt clears up the old rumor that he chased Tyler Perry with a broomstick:
Mike Epps: “You know, Eddie Murphy told me a story. He said,…
— The Art Of Dialogue (@ArtOfDialogue_) November 14, 2026 
 Epps recalled a story Eddie Murphy told him about the time Suge Knight and Katt Williams popped up at Murphy’s house, adding that he wished he could have been a fly on the wall. “How did y’all get over there?” Epps asked.
 “As a Jehovah’s Witness,” Williams replied through laughter. “I don’t know why Eddie Murphy told that story. He know exactly what—don’t let somebody tell you a story where [it’s like], ‘Oh, I just woke up and some scary individuals was there!’”
 Immediately after, Epps brought up rumors that Williams once chased Tyler Perry with a broomstick. “Tyler Perry is six-foot-six. I ain’t chase [him],” Williams added.
 Where He Stands With Cedric the Entertainer
 On Club Shay Shay, Williams claimed he performed a joke in 1998 on BET’s “ComicView” that he says “The Original Kings of Comedy” star stole from him. 
 “I’m not gonna say nothing funny to Cedric,” Williams told Epps when asked how he would reply to a greeting. “I got 19 assault and batteries. I’m either gon’ go the opposite direction of Cedric when I see him, or I’ma be up on him before he know it.” Epps replied: “I believe you!”
 His Past 14 Gun Charges
 Mike Epps and Ice Cube ask Katt Williams about his past 14 gun charges and rumors of him fighting after shows—prompting Mike Epps to reveal Katt once pulled a gun on him and chased him down the street:
Mike Epps: “You put the guns in there?”
Katt Williams: “Yup, the 14 gun…
— The Art Of Dialogue (@ArtOfDialogue_) November 15, 2026 
 Speaking of assaults and batteries, Williams also opened up about the criminal charges he detailed in his debut memoir, “Nine Lives, No Wives, and 69 Concubines.”
 “The 14 gun charges in New York City, going to Rikers Island, yeah I was very transparent,” Williams said before Ice Cube recalled hearing how Williams had beat somebody up in an alleyway. 
 “Everything you’ve heard about this nigga he did it. Let’s get that out the way,” Epps said. “I have also been a victim of his before. He also pulled a gun on me before, chasing me down the street.” Williams clarified Epps wasn’t alone, claiming Faizon [Love] was also apart of the ordeal.
